also: you’ll be the death of me

terms.gloss: you’re killing me: you plague me to death
evidence: Plaut. Merc. 157: lassitūdinem hercle verba tua mihi addunt, ēnicās
Plaut. Merc. 893: ēnicās mē miserum tuā reticentiā
terms.comment: From ēnecō (ēnicō), kill off. “Especially frequent: ēnicās or ēnicās mē” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quid tacēs? dīc. ēnicās mē miserum tuā reticentiā.
phrases.english: Why don’t you speak? Tell me. You’re killing me with your silence.

phrases.latin: lassitūdinem hercle verba tua mihi addunt, ēnicās
phrases.english: your words only make me more tired, by Hercules; you’re killing me

sources: Lewis & Short: eneco
